newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end down, but escape Dow's fall.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end down, but escape Dow's fall.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 19697.17 -156.72 LME CASH NICKEL US$6751 -54.0
CANDLR 1.3740 LME CASH ALUM US$1528.0 -40.0
CAN 30-YR 118.59 +0.35 BRENT CRUDE US$18.22 -0.16
* Toronto stocks ended softer on Wednesday but escaped New York's tumble. * Buoyed by firmer forestry, industrial products. * 109 million shares traded worth C$1.8 billion.
Metz has predicted that Toronto would extend its recent rally amid a global industrial boom that would benefit its heavyweight natural resource groups.
Gold bullion prices resumed their dive after Tuesday's marginal bounce, pressuring Toronto's influential gold sector. The key Comex price slipped $2.10 to reach $318.90, near 12-year lows again.
But "even though gold was down, there were still a couple of bright spots," a trader said.
They included six of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors, which added points. Forestry products, industrial products and utilities led the way.
Conglomerates, consumer products and media weakened along with golds.
Trading was heavy at 109 million shares worth C$1.8 billion. Declining issues outpaced advances 583 to 424, with 295 flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Steelmaker IPSCO Inc rose 2.20 to 44 after announcing details of a large pipe order totalling 180,000 tons.
* IPL Energy Inc rose 1.55 to 49.40 in moderate trade as investors approved of IPL's purchase of a 32-percent stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc.

* Battered paper maker Repap Enterprises Inc rose 0.12 to 0.50 in trading of more than 3.7 million shares. It agreed to sell its Repap USA unit to Consolidated Papers Inc for $674 million. The company said creditors agreed to extend the July 31 due date on C$270 million of its bank debt into its third quarter after the news.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
